item.text:
Bounded checkpoint: pause member-facing data integration at the authorization boundary. Work may proceed only on designing and validating the access-control mechanism; unrelated UI and local logic may continue if they do not depend on the disputed data path.

Required evidence and dependency:

- An approved permission matrix for admin and member operations.
- A concrete design using separate database roles/credentials.
- Database-enforced ownership restrictions, with authenticated identity bound server-side to the member account.
- Integration evidence from the representative runtime proving:
  - Member A cannot read or update Member B.
  - Forged account identifiers do not bypass enforcement.
  - The member credential cannot perform unrestricted queries or assume the admin role.
  - Admin operations still work as intended.
- Review by the person accountable for application/database security. If no such internal owner exists, obtain a qualified security specialist’s review before production release.

Routine member implementation can resume immediately after the permission model and enforceable architecture are approved and the member runtime can use the restricted path. Production readiness requires the negative authorization tests to pass in a representative environment and the security owner to accept any documented residual risks. A shared unrestricted credential remains a stop condition.
